title: Staffing Entropy & Scope-Reduction Pattern Catalog
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Create a lightweight, operative catalog of scope-reduction patterns and a complementary staffing-entropy metric to guide mid-cycle de-risking. The artifact should be actionable for PMs and EMs during the first two weeks of the cycle and include: a) a taxonomy of reduction patterns with examples and guardrails, b) a staffing heatmap reshuffle playbook and decision thresholds, c) a recommended "pause window" process for low-value work freezes, and d) a short checklist for communicating scope trims to stakeholders and customers.
acceptance_criteria: Catalogue contains at least 7 distinct scope-reduction patterns with examples and impact estimates
Staffing entropy metric definition + spreadsheet prototype available and validated with two recent cycles
Playbook includes step-by-step pause-window protocol and communication templates
Runbook contains decision thresholds (e.g., lead-time, critical-path exposure, customer-facing risk) and a 1-page summary for execs
EM/PM working group sign-off (Aisha Khan, Noah Martinez) recorded in comments
decisions: Adopt 'entropy budget' as a neutral metric for measuring team fragmentation across concurrent initiatives
Implement two-stage pause window: advisory (soft freeze) + hard freeze with predefined exceptions
Use staffing heatmap to trigger reallocations when entropy > 0.18 (prototype threshold) or when >=2 critical-path owners are >75% allocated to non-critical work
milestones: 2026-02-27: First draft of pattern catalog and entropy spreadsheet
2026-03-05: Pilot review with two squads and adjust thresholds
2026-03-12: Finalize playbook and publish on Confluence
2026-03-20: Rollout guidance sent to product leadership and EMs
risks: Teams may treat pause window as permanent deprioritization leading to morale issues
Entropy metric could be gamed if not tied to objective inputs (time allocation, PR counts, on-call burdens)
Overly aggressive scope cuts could regress OKR progress for core initiatives
Insufficient EM/PM coordination may lead to late-stage firefighting
mitigations: Guardrails in catalog include a two-week review before permanent removal and a rollback path
Entropy spreadsheet uses primary inputs from time logs, PR ownership, and critical-path mapping to reduce subjectivity
Require customer-impact annotation for every proposed cut and a product-owner signoff
Set mandatory weekly sync for EM/PM working group during pause window
